title: NBA Offseason Daily Digest
subtitle: July 31, 2026 - Roster Moves, Blockbuster Deals & Documentary Buzz

items.headline: LeBron James Set for 'Last Dance'-Style Documentary with 76ers
items.summary: NBA icon LeBron James and ESPN are reportedly finalizing a behind-the-scenes documentary akin to 'The Last Dance', chronicling his final chapter with the Philadelphia 76ers. James, who signed a two-year, $8 million deal this offseason, aims for a fifth NBA title in what is expected to be his 24th and final season.

items.headline: Blockbuster: Giannis Antetokounmpo Traded to Miami Heat
items.summary: In a seismic offseason move, the Milwaukee Bucks have traded two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat. The Bucks received a significant package including Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakučionis, the No. 13 pick in the 2026 draft, first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, a 2030 pick swap, and a 2033 second-round pick.

items.headline: Kawhi Leonard Trade to Raptors on Hold Amid NBA Investigation
items.summary: The highly anticipated trade sending Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors is currently stalled, with the Raptors reportedly refusing to finalize the deal. Toronto is wary of inheriting potential NBA penalties stemming from an ongoing investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers. Despite the delay, the trade, which would bring the 35-year-old Leonard to the Raptors, is still expected to be completed before the 2026-27 season, possibly with amendments.

items.headline: Nets Acquire Julius Randle in Three-Team Deal
items.summary: The Brooklyn Nets have acquired forward Julius Randle and the No. 28 pick in the 2026 draft as part of a three-team trade. The Minnesota Timberwolves sent Randle to Brooklyn, receiving Mo Gueye and the No. 33 pick. The Chicago Bulls landed center Nic Claxton in the transaction.

items.headline: Kings Open to Moving Zach LaVine After Picking Up Option
items.summary: Zach LaVine's future with the Sacramento Kings remains uncertain, despite him picking up his $49 million player option. Reports indicate the Kings have informed LaVine that a starting role or long-term commitment is not guaranteed, leaving open the possibility of a trade for the guard who has been a frequent subject of offseason speculation.

items.headline: Hawks Acquire Aaron Wiggins from Thunder
items.summary: The Atlanta Hawks have completed a deal to acquire guard Aaron Wiggins from the Oklahoma City Thunder. In exchange, the Thunder will receive a 2030 second-round pick and a 2032 second-round pick.

items.headline: James Harden Poised to Re-Sign with Cavaliers
items.summary: Veteran guard James Harden is expected to re-sign with the Cleveland Cavaliers, despite declining his $42.3 million player option for the 2026-27 season. The strategic delay in his new contract allows the Cavaliers flexibility to pursue further roster enhancements.

items.headline: Cavaliers Still Eyeing Restricted Free Agent Peyton Watson
items.summary: Restricted free agent Peyton Watson remains a target for the Cleveland Cavaliers, though a deal would necessitate a sign-and-trade with the Denver Nuggets. Negotiations between Watson and Denver are reportedly stalled, as the 23-year-old seeks a contract with a higher annual value than Christian Braun's recent extension.

items.headline: Wizards' Jamir Watkins Suffers Torn ACL in Summer League
items.summary: Washington Wizards guard Jamir Watkins is facing a significant recovery period after undergoing surgery to repair a torn ACL in his left knee. Watkins sustained the injury during the team's NBA Summer League opener, sidelining him for the remainder of the tournament.

items.headline: Josh Richardson Retires After 10-Year NBA Career
items.summary: After a decade in the league, Josh Richardson has announced his retirement at 32 years old. Richardson played for multiple teams throughout his career, most recently with the New Orleans Pelicans in the 2023-24 season.

items.headline: Offseason Coaching Carousel Continues
items.summary: The coaching landscape saw several significant changes this offseason. Jamahl Mosley, formerly with Orlando, was hired as the new head coach for the New Orleans Pelicans on May 18, 2026. Sean Sweeney took the helm for the Orlando Magic on June 1, 2026. The Chicago Bulls hired Tiago Splitter on June 16, 2026, while Micah Nori joined the Portland Trail Blazers on June 23, 2026, and Dusty May became the new head coach for the Dallas Mavericks on the same day.
